raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year. It's spring now — my wheat's been in the ground since mid-October last year, so that one's already going. I need to plan out the spring topdressing and irrigation for it, get the cotton ready to plant in about a month, and then think ahead to the maize that goes in right after wheat harvest in June.

My land is 10.1 mu total. Like most years, I split it — 6 mu for the wheat-maize double crop on the better ground near the house where I can get water easy, and the other 4.1 mu is cotton on the sandier plot my mother-in-law's family used to farm. I've been doing it this way for maybe eight years now and it works. The wheat-maize brings in steady grain for the family and a bit to sell, and the cotton brings cash if the price is decent.

My husband works construction in town most of the year, so it's me and my mother-in-law mostly, plus the kids help during cotton picking when school's out. That matters — cotton is the hard one for labor. If I had more cotton I couldn't manage it.

**On the wheat** — it looked okay coming out of winter, not the best stand but not bad. I put down about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu when I planted in October, that's the 15-15-15. Now at jointing, probably late March or early April, I'll topdress with urea — around 15 kg per mu. Some folks in the village do 20 kg but I've found 15 is enough on my ground, and urea's not cheap. If the wheat looks pale at booting I'll add a little more but usually I don't. I'll irrigate at jointing, heading, and then once more at grain filling if it stays dry — three times most years. Last year we got lucky with rain and I only irrigated twice, saved some money. My neighbor Wang uses four times but his yield isn't really better than mine, so I stick with three.

**On the cotton** — I'll plant mid to late April, depends on the soil temperature. I use the Bt variety seed from the co-op, it handles the bollworm better so I don't have to spray as much. Costs around 40 yuan per mu for seed. Before planting I put down compound fertilizer, about 40 kg per mu, and I topdress with urea at squaring and again at boll setting — around 10 kg each time. Cotton needs more than the grain crops really, but I try not to overdo it because too much nitrogen makes it grow tall and leafy without setting bolls. My cousin who farms over in Nanhu village told me that years back and it stuck with me. Cotton takes more spraying too — I'll do the bollworm sprays in July-August even with Bt seed, and something for aphids early on. That's the expensive part.

**On the maize** — I'll plant right after wheat harvest, usually June 12-15, whatever day we can get the combine and the planter in. It's tight, only about 3-4 days between. I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whichever the co-op has. I broadcast compound fertilizer before planting, 30 kg per mu, and topdress urea at the big flare stage around 12 kg. Maize doesn't need much irrigation if the summer rain comes — usually one time at tasseling if it's dry. Some years I don't irrigate at all.

Cost-wise I'm looking at maybe 4,000-4,500 yuan for the whole season. That's manageable. Main worry is if cotton price drops again or if we get hail in August — then the cotton's gone and I've already put all the inputs in.
